formalization.definitions:
namespace PV

/-- Terms of Cook's theory `PV` over the sort of finite Boolean strings:
variables, the empty string `ε`, the two successors `s₀, s₁`, concatenation
`∘`, smash `#`, trim-right `TR` and iterated trim `ITR`. -/
inductive Term : Type
  | var : ℕ → Term
  | eps : Term
  | s0 : Term → Term
  | s1 : Term → Term
  | concat : Term → Term → Term
  | smash : Term → Term → Term
  | TR : Term → Term
  | ITR : Term → Term → Term

open Term

/-- Simultaneous substitution of variables by terms. -/
def subst (σ : ℕ → Term) : Term → Term
  | var n => σ n
  | eps => eps
  | s0 t => s0 (subst σ t)
  | s1 t => s1 (subst σ t)
  | concat t1 t2 => concat (subst σ t1) (subst σ t2)
  | smash t1 t2 => smash (subst σ t1) (subst σ t2)
  | TR t => TR (subst σ t)
  | ITR t1 t2 => ITR (subst σ t1) (subst σ t2)

/-- Substitute a single variable `n` by the term `t` inside `u`. -/
def substOne (n : ℕ) (t : Term) (u : Term) : Term :=
  subst (fun m => if m = n then t else var m) u

/-- The equational derivability relation `PV ⊢ t₁ = t₂`. It captures the
logical rules (L0) reflexivity, (L1) symmetry, (L2) transitivity,
(L3) congruence, (L4) substitution, the defining axioms of the base
functions, and the structural-induction rule. In the induction rule,
`var 0` plays the role of the recursion variable `y`, `var 1` plays the
role of the recursive-call variable `z` occurring in `h_i`, and all other
variables uniformly play the role of the parameter tuple `x` (they are
left untouched by the two designated substitutions). -/
inductive Deriv : Term → Term → Prop
  | refl (t : Term) : Deriv t t
  | symm {t1 t2} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv t2 t1
  | trans {t1 t2 t3} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv t2 t3 → Deriv t1 t3
  | congr_s0 {t1 t2} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv (s0 t1) (s0 t2)
  | congr_s1 {t1 t2} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv (s1 t1) (s1 t2)
  | congr_concat {t1 t2 t3 t4} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv t3 t4 →
      Deriv (concat t1 t3) (concat t2 t4)
  | congr_smash {t1 t2 t3 t4} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv t3 t4 →
      Deriv (smash t1 t3) (smash t2 t4)
  | congr_TR {t1 t2} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv (TR t1) (TR t2)
  | congr_ITR {t1 t2 t3 t4} : Deriv t1 t2 → Deriv t3 t4 →
      Deriv (ITR t1 t3) (ITR t2 t4)
  | substRule {t1 t2} (σ : ℕ → Term) : Deriv t1 t2 →
      Deriv (subst σ t1) (subst σ t2)
  | ax_concat_eps : Deriv (concat (var 0) eps) (var 0)
  | ax_concat_s0 : Deriv (concat (var 0) (s0 (var 1))) (s0 (concat (var 0) (var 1)))
  | ax_concat_s1 : Deriv (concat (var 0) (s1 (var 1))) (s1 (concat (var 0) (var 1)))
  | ax_TR_eps : Deriv (TR eps) eps
  | ax_TR_s0 : Deriv (TR (s0 (var 0))) (var 0)
  | ax_TR_s1 : Deriv (TR (s1 (var 0))) (var 0)
  | ax_ITR_eps : Deriv (ITR (var 0) eps) (var 0)
  | ax_ITR_s0 : Deriv (ITR (var 0) (s0 (var 1))) (TR (ITR (var 0) (var 1)))
  | ax_ITR_s1 : Deriv (ITR (var 0) (s1 (var 1))) (TR (ITR (var 0) (var 1)))
  | ax_smash_eps : Deriv (smash (var 0) eps) eps
  | ax_smash_s0 : Deriv (smash (var 0) (s0 (var 1))) (concat (var 0) (smash (var 0) (var 1)))
  | ax_smash_s1 : Deriv (smash (var 0) (s1 (var 1))) (concat (var 0) (smash (var 0) (var 1)))
  | ind {p q g h0 h1 : Term} :
      Deriv (substOne 0 eps p) g →
      Deriv (substOne 0 eps q) g →
      Deriv (substOne 0 (s0 (var 0)) p) (substOne 1 p h0) →
      Deriv (substOne 0 (s1 (var 0)) p) (substOne 1 p h1) →
      Deriv (substOne 0 (s0 (var 0)) q) (substOne 1 q h0) →
      Deriv (substOne 0 (s1 (var 0)) q) (substOne 1 q h1) →
      Deriv p q

/-- The function `f₁(x,y) := ITR(ε, x ∘ y)`, introduced by composition from
`ITR`, the constant `ε`, and concatenation, as used in this part of the
proof (it is the function whose base case `f₁(z,ε) = ε` is established
here). -/
def f1 (x y : Term) : Term := ITR eps (concat x y)

end PV
formalization.signature: : ∀ z : Term, Deriv (f1 z eps) eps
formalization.notes: The term algebra of $\{0,1\}^*$ (variables, $\eps$, $s_0,s_1$, $\circ$, $\#$, $\TR$, $\ITR$) is encoded by the inductive type `Term`, and the defining axioms $x\circ\eps=x$, $x\circ s_i(y)=s_i(x\circ y)$, $\TR(\eps)=\eps$, $\TR(s_i(x))=x$, $\ITR(x,\eps)=x$, $\ITR(x,s_i(y))=\TR(\ITR(x,y))$, $x\#\eps=\eps$, $x\#s_i(y)=x\circ(x\#y)$ become the `ax_*` constructors of `Deriv`, using `var 0`/`var 1` as schematic variables that are later instantiated via the substitution rule `substRule`. The logical apparatus (L0)–(L4) is given by `refl`, `symm`, `trans`, the `congr_*` constructors (one per function symbol) and `substRule`, using the generic simultaneous substitution operator `subst`/`substOne`. The structural-induction rule of the source (`f_j(\vec x,\eps)=g(\vec x)$ and $f_j(\vec x,s_i(y))=h_i(\vec x,y,f_j(\vec x,y))$ for $j=1,2$ imply $f_1=f_2$) is the `ind` constructor, where `var 0` stands for the induction variable $y$, `var 1` for the recursive-value variable $z$ occurring inside $h_i$, and all remaining free variables uniformly stand for the untouched parameter tuple $\vec x$. The specific function $f_1$ used in this proposition, introduced by composition as $\ITR(\eps, x\circ y)$ (matching the informal proof's identification of $f_1(z,\eps)$ with $\ITR(\eps,z\circ\eps)$), is given by the definition `f1`. Finally, `PV ⊢ f_1(z,\eps)=\eps$` is rendered as `∀ z : Term, Deriv (f1 z eps) eps`, universally quantifying over the free variable $z$ of the source equation, as is standard for equations in an equational calculus with a substitution rule.
formalization.readback:
For every term $z$, the following equation is derivable in Cook's theory $\text{PV}$:

$$\text{ITR}(\varepsilon, z \circ \varepsilon) = \varepsilon$$

where $\varepsilon$ is the empty string, $\circ$ denotes concatenation, and $\text{ITR}$ is the iterated trim operation. Derivability is the inductive relation $\text{Deriv}(t_1, t_2)$, defined through reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity, congruence for each operator, substitution, the defining axioms of the base functions, and the structural-induction rule.
formalization.issues: None. The `Deriv` relation correctly encodes the logical rules (L0)–(L4), the defining axioms of `∘`, `TR`, `ITR`, `#`, and the structural-induction rule (with `var 0` uniformly playing the role of the recursion variable `y` and `var 1` the role of the recursive-call slot `z`, matching the source's schema with two base-case/two recursive-case premises for `j=1,2`). The definition `f1 x y := ITR eps (concat x y)` matches exactly the term the informal proof itself reduces the goal to (`ITR(ε, z∘ε) = ε`), so the Lean goal `Deriv (f1 z eps) eps` is definitionally the same equation as `f₁(z,ε) = ε` unfolded, consistent with what the source proof establishes. Universally quantifying over `z : Term` is equivalent to (and derivable from) the free-variable formulation in the source via the substitution rule (L4), so no strengthening or weakening occurs. The readback accurately reflects what the Lean statement asserts.

sketch.main_proof:
intro z
unfold f1
exact Deriv.trans (Deriv.congr_ITR (Deriv.refl eps) (concat_eps_subst z)) (ITR_eps_subst z)

lemmas.name: concat_eps_subst
lemmas.statement: theorem concat_eps_subst (z : Term) : Deriv (concat z eps) z
lemmas.proof: exact Deriv.substRule (fun n => if n = 0 then z else var n) Deriv.ax_concat_eps

lemmas.name: ITR_eps_var_eps
lemmas.proof:
refine @Deriv.ind (ITR eps (var 0)) eps eps (TR (var 1)) (TR (var 1)) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
· -- Base case for p: Deriv (ITR eps eps) eps
  exact Deriv.substRule (fun m => if m = 0 then eps else var m) Deriv.ax_ITR_eps
· -- Base case for q: Deriv eps eps
  exact Deriv.refl eps
· -- Recursive s0 for p: Deriv (ITR eps (s0 (var 0))) (TR (ITR eps (var 0)))
  have h : Deriv (ITR eps (s0 (var 1))) (TR (ITR eps (var 1))) := 
    Deriv.substRule (fun m => if m = 0 then eps else var m) Deriv.ax_ITR_s0
  exact Deriv.substRule (fun m => if m = 1 then var 0 else var m) h
· -- Recursive s1 for p: Deriv (ITR eps (s1 (var 0))) (TR (ITR eps (var 0)))
  have h : Deriv (ITR eps (s1 (var 1))) (TR (ITR eps (var 1))) := 
    Deriv.substRule (fun m => if m = 0 then eps else var m) Deriv.ax_ITR_s1
  exact Deriv.substRule (fun m => if m = 1 then var 0 else var m) h
· -- Recursive s0 for q: Deriv eps (TR eps)
  exact Deriv.symm Deriv.ax_TR_eps
· -- Recursive s1 for q: Deriv eps (TR eps)
  exact Deriv.symm Deriv.ax_TR_eps
